questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(4,15,-5)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $(r-[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 9 \\ 2\end{aligned}])\cdot [\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=0.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(6,9,2).$ Then 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 9 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 15 \\ -5\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -6 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector $n=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|2\cdot (-5)+(-6)\cdot 1+7\cdot (-2)|}{\sqrt{(-5)^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-10-6-14|}{\sqrt{25+1+4}} \\  & =\frac{|-30|}{\sqrt{30}} \\  & =\sqrt{30}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-2,11,1)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $r\cdot ⟨2,-5,4⟩=20.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a point on the plane. If $r=⟨x,y,z⟩,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨2,-5,4⟩ & =20 \\ 2x-5y+4z & =20 \\ 4z & =20-2x+5y \\ z & =5-\frac{1}{2}x+\frac{5}{4}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $x=2$ and $y=4,$ we get 

$$
z=5-\frac{1}{2}(2)+\frac{5}{4}(4)=9.
$$

So, the point $Q(2,4,9)$ lies on the plane. 

Now, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,4,9⟩-⟨-2,11,1⟩ \\  & =⟨4,-7,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨2,-5,4⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(4)\cdot 2+(-7)\cdot (-5)+8\cdot 4|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|8+35+32|}{\sqrt{4+25+16}} \\  & =\frac{|75|}{\sqrt{45}} \\  & =5\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|2\cdot (-3)+5\cdot 2+6\cdot 3|}{\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-6+10+18|}{\sqrt{9+4+9}} \\  & =\frac{|22|}{\sqrt{22}} \\  & =\sqrt{22}\end{aligned}

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-7,5,2)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $4x-8y+8z=-36.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=-1$ and $y=1$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-8y+8z & =-36 \\ 4(-1)-8(1)+8z & =-36 \\ 8z & =-24 \\ z & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(-1,1,-3)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-1,1,-3⟩-⟨-7,5,2⟩ \\  & =⟨6,-4,-5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨4,-8,8⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|6\cdot 4+(-4)\cdot (-8)+(-5)\cdot 8|}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+(-8)^{2}+{8}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|24+32-40|}{\sqrt{16+64+64}} \\  & =\frac{|\,16\,|}{\sqrt{144}} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,-2,-1⟩-⟨0,-1,2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $\mathbf{n}= \langle 2, 0, -2 \rangle.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|1\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 0+(-3)\cdot (-2)|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|2+0+6|}{\sqrt{4+0+4}} \\  & =\frac{|\,8\,|}{\sqrt{8}} \\  & =\sqrt{8} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Shortest Distance Between a Point and a Plane Given in Cartesian Form
canonical_examples.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(3 , -10 , 3)$ and the plane $\Pi$ with equation $2x+y-2z = -1$.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=4$ and $y=-5$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+y-2z & =-1 \\ 2(4)+(-5)+1 & =2z \\ 4 & =2z \\ z & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(4, -5, 2)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overrightarrow{PQ},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨4,-5,2⟩-⟨3,-10,3⟩ \\  & =⟨1,5,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $\mathbf{n}=\langle a,b,c \rangle.$ So, for the plane $\Pi,$ we have $\mathbf{n}= \langle 2, 1, -2 \rangle.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|1\cdot 2+5\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-2)|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|2+5+2|}{\sqrt{4+1+4}} \\  & =\frac{|\,9\,|}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$
